original_question: If a II1 factor M is McDuff and decomposes as M congruent N1 tensor N2, determine whether at least one tensor factor N1 or N2 must also be McDuff.
target_in_paper: Problem 21 in the section "McDuff and Property Gamma factors": for a tensor decomposition of II_1 factors M = N \bar\otimes P, if M is McDuff, must one of N or P be McDuff? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact mathematical core of Problem 21: the ambient setting is II_1 factors, the hypothesis is that a tensor product factor is McDuff, and the conclusion being asked about is whether one tensor factor must itself be McDuff. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
missing_details: The tensor product should be the von Neumann/spatial tensor product, written \bar\otimes, rather than an unspecified tensor product. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))

The factors N_1 and N_2 should be stated explicitly to be II_1 factors, since the paper formulates the question in the II_1-factor setting and does not broaden it beyond that section. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))

To make the question stand alone, it helps to define "McDuff" as absorbing the hyperfinite II_1 factor R, i.e. M \cong M \bar\otimes R. The paper uses the term without redefinition in Problem 21 because the section is addressed to specialists. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
The paper states this as an open implication question ("does it imply") rather than as a request to solve or classify the situation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))

No extra assumptions such as separability, Connes embeddability, fullness, or property Gamma are included in Problem 21, so a paper-faithful rewrite should not add them. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
refined_question: Let M, N_1, and N_2 be II_1 factors, and suppose that M \cong N_1 \bar\otimes N_2, where \bar\otimes denotes the spatial von Neumann tensor product. If M is McDuff (equivalently, M \cong M \bar\otimes R for the hyperfinite II_1 factor R), must at least one of the tensor factors N_1 or N_2 be McDuff? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of Problem 21 and does not seem to target any neighboring question. The only real gaps are the precise tensor-product notation, the explicit statement that all algebras involved are II_1 factors, and a standalone reminder of what "McDuff" means. The nearby paper context adds only that this belongs to the section on "McDuff and Property Gamma factors" and that the author notes a partial result in reference [26]; it does not supply an equivalent reformulation or extra hypotheses. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
